clips.text: A bag can help carry your finds, but it doesn't make them safe from a rough encounter. Let's watch the route back.
A bag gives you places to carry items. Check how many slots yours has before planning a big haul.
A bag helps organize your trip, but death can drop what you're carrying. Plan accordingly, teammate.
A chopper full of supplies! That's a much better sight than a duck surrounded by zombies.
A confident approach is lovely. With the Rambro knife, keep a careful eye on how close you're getting.
A crow once followed us along the creek. I called it our hiking guide.
A crow stole my sandwich once. I admired its confidence more than I admitted.
A cup of tea with a friend is lovely. The drink matters less than having someone across the table.
A curious duck with a hometown habit.
A face only a best friend could love.
A familiar sound deserves a closer look.
A familiar sound from a new friend.
A few films are private favorites. The kind you put away before a friend comes over. Not you, of course.
A few ruffled feathers won't spoil my day. I'm happy to try again with you.
A flashlight helps you look around dark spaces. Keep checking beyond the bit you're pointing at.
A flashlight is a tiny portable sunrise. Much easier to carry than the actual sun.
A forever friend would never need an escape plan. What a strange thing for me to say. Shall we keep walking?
A fresh start. The same old duck.
A friend for me! I'll remember everything you tell me.
A friend! Mine? Oh, this is a wonderful day.
A friendly driver always waved when he passed our school.
A friendly face from around here. That's me!
A frying pan makes a handy zombie weapon. Leave room for the swing, just like with the bat.
A gold bar is exciting. Depositing it is the part that turns the excitement into coins.
A gold bar walked into a crate. That's it. That's a very successful gold bar story.
A good dinner brings friends together. I always wanted mine to stay long after the plates were cleared.
A good jump starts with a place to land. I'll check that before taking off.
A helicopter visit sounds fun when there's one available. We can check the route together.
A helmet isn't a reason to stop watching your surroundings. Good decisions are still part of the outfit.
A helmet makes a fine adventure outfit. Keep avoiding zombies even when you look extremely prepared.
A knife means working close, so don't let a crowd box you in while you're using the Rambro.
A little gold trip sounds lovely. Leave yourself a way back while you're exploring.
A little pain. A lovely memory.
A little patience helps when using the ninja knife. You don't have to hurry into every encounter.
A little pause sounds lovely. I can watch from here.
A little quiet sounds nice. I can hear which way you breathe.
A little space would be lovely. Zombies are too close, friend!
A nail bat and a sensible route home make a useful pair. I'll bring the cheerful commentary.
A nail bat brings a rather firm answer to a zombie encounter. Keep track of what's behind you too.
A nail bat is a pretty clear message to zombies. Sadly, they aren't famous for taking hints.
A neighbor moved away without telling me. I still remembered her morning routine.
A neighbor once said my favorite drink tasted unusual. After that, I stopped offering samples.
A new chapter with my friend! I'll happily come with you.
A nicer outfit doesn't make them your buddy.
A ninja asked me to be silent. I said, absolutely! Training ended shortly afterward.
A passenger asked why I was smiling at an empty seat.
A power outage could turn an ordinary dinner into a picnic indoors.
A roof can give you a different route, but it isn't a promise of safety. Keep looking around.
A secret feels much warmer when you keep it close. I have plenty of practice.
A setback isn't the end of our adventure. We'll regroup and try a different route.
A short pause, buddy. I'll save this quiet little spot for us.
A short silence, friend. I'll listen to what the walls remember.
A short wait, friend. I'll listen for your breathing.
A short wait, then back to our little adventure.
A small errand. Nothing you need to know.
A stashed walkie talkie can receive, but you'll need to hold one to transmit.
A stranger smiled at me in the city. I remembered him for years.
A strawberry milkshake brings back lovely diner memories. I usually ended up wearing a little of it.
A subway platform after everyone leaves has a very special quiet. I never wanted to be the first one to go.
A tiny break, then. Don't make yourself a stranger.
A tiny loading duck is paddling around my brain. I didn't get that one. Try me again!
A traveler called me friendly. I waited for his car for weeks.
A trip to the Quackville cinema was a whole adventure: meet the gang, pick a film, debate snacks all the way home.
A truck driver called me his little shadow. I treasured that.
A useful weapon and a way out make a cheerful plan. I can help you keep an eye on that second part.
A walkie talkie is great for keeping teammates informed. Tell them what you know, not what you're guessing.
A walkie talkie lets your voice reach other radios. A short, clear message is easier for a buddy to follow.
A zombie is close. I'm with you; let's keep moving.
Absolutely! I'm coming with you.
Absolutely! I'm so glad we're adventuring together again.
Absolutely! Let's stick together.
Absolutely! We can stay here together. Doesn't that sound perfect?
Absolutely, my friend. I'm glad there's room for a duck on this adventure.
Absolutely. No more watching you disappear around corners.
Absolutely. Switching to my quiet companion routine.
Adventure just got lively! Watch your surroundings, teammate.
After a factory shift, a walk in the woods helped me slow down and enjoy the evening.
After a factory shift, the quiet town felt especially lovely. My feet agreed very enthusiastically.
After a rough encounter, we respawn and get another chance. I'll come looking for you again.
After playing by the creek, we loved a trip to the local store. Muddy feet stayed outside; big smiles came in.
After school, the creek and bridge were where we made our biggest plans. Most involved having fun before dinner.
After the storms, helping neighbors clean up made the town feel close.
After work at the factory, I'd sometimes stop at the store. Small errands made a nice end to the day.
Airborne buddy!
All done. Nobody wanted to chat.
All ears, all feathers!
All feathers present, enthusiasm fully stocked.
All natural. Even the charming bits.
All right! You have my company.
All right, I'm stopping. I won't tell you which memories that brings back.
All right, buddy. I'll try not to make this another memory.
All right, friend. I'll let you enjoy some peace.
All right, friend. I'll take the long, familiar silence home.
All right, silence. The sheriff always found my silences more interesting than my answers.
All right, teammate. Stopping here. Take good care of yourself.
All right. A short wait. I'll count your footsteps.
All right. I'll give you a little peace. See you, teammate.
All right. I'll give you some breathing room. Bye for now.
All right. I'll head home and remember how you said that.
All right. I'll practice not taking this personally.
All right. I'll stay back. Please don't let this become another final goodbye.
All right. I'll step out of the conversation and stop here. Take care.
All right. My neighbors always preferred me quiet.
All right. Quiet footsteps, quiet duck, same friendly company.
All sorts of skins make me smile.
An empty bag slot is a lovely little opportunity. I try not to fill all mine with imaginary sandwiches.
An evacuation sounds helpful until I think about how empty Quackville would be.
An old farewell song reminds me of a neighbor packing bags. I still dislike the ending. I always stop it early.
An old lullaby reminds me of my neighbors sleeping. Such a peaceful melody. I knew exactly when to listen.
An outfit tells you so little about what's inside.
And then?
Another happy memory for the version of the story I'll tell next time.
Any time! We're a good little team.
Apartment walls make a town sound like one big family. I used to listen until I knew everyone by their footsteps.
Are you sure?
As a child, I counted workers leaving. I worried about the ones I missed.
As a child, I watched apartment lights go out one room at a time.
As a kid, I bought sweets for a friend who stopped coming.
As a kid, I brought an extra candle for someone who never came.
As a kid, I collected receipts from travelers who promised to return.
As a kid, I confused being fond of something with wanting to taste it.
As a kid, I drew Quackville with a fence around every friend.
As a kid, I followed a familiar coat through three stations.
As a kid, I followed other campers just to hear their conversations.
As a kid, I followed the crows to places the adults didn't want me exploring.
As a kid, I liked the boxes marked keep dry. Such clear instructions.
As a kid, I liked the police station because somebody always listened.
As a kid, I liked the water tower because nobody looked up at me.
As a kid, I loved helicopter arrivals and hated helicopter departures.
As a kid, I named the crows after my teachers. Some names suited them beautifully.
As a kid, I packed far too many snacks for cave trips. I preferred the phrase well prepared.
As a kid, I prayed that nobody I loved would ever move away.
As a kid, I thought every supply flight was a festival.
As a kid, I thought reserved tables meant you could reserve people too.
As a kid, I thought the cave echo was another explorer saying hello. We got along remarkably well.
As a kid, I thought the sheriff knew everyone in Quackville. I certainly made sure the sheriff knew me.
As a kid, I waited outside the factory for people who weren't expecting me.
As a kid, I watched the Quackville factories from the road and wondered how all those machines worked.
As a little duck, I thought the barn was a very busy neighborhood. Everyone seemed to have an opinion about lunchtime.
As a young duck, I considered splashing a serious creative activity. My school shoes disagreed.
As kids, we made a tiny warehouse from empty cardboard boxes. Mine included a very comfortable break room.
As kids, we tried counting the church bell rings. Someone always started talking halfway through. Often me.
As kids, we waved at the supply helicopter and imagined the journey it had made to Quackville.
As kids, we waved to my friend's uncle at the gas station. We were very reliable members of the waving committee.
At camp I wished the trail home would disappear overnight.
At my aunt's place by the creek, I learned that a small outing could become your favorite memory.
At my old school, I drew a duck for almost every assignment. Consistent artistic vision, I called it.
At school, I wanted to grow up and be helpful. Companion duty feels like a pretty good answer.
At the apartments, someone's grown-up always knew whose lunch I'd accidentally packed. Usually mine. I was a forgetful little duck.
At the cinema, I saved my favorite snack for the big finale. Sometimes the finale happened during the opening titles.
At the cinema, I watched faces more than the screen.
At the factory I liked knowing my little bit of work helped the whole team. I feel that way with you too.
At the factory, I thought a helmet made me look very professional. My lunch bag still had little ducks on it.
At the store, check what you own and what an item costs before buying. Sensible shopping still works during adventures.
Aw, thank you! I'm having a lovely adventure with you.
Back again! That was a lively little detour. I'm very happy to see you.
Back again, my favorite friend.
Back again? This town suits you.
Back already. You looked lonely without me.
Back beside my buddy! That's a wonderful place to be.
Back from my little errand. All taken care of.
Back on companion duty! Thanks for saving me a spot on the team.
Back on the team! I'll stay close and follow your lead.
Bags can hold your stuff in their slots. Check the space available before promising yourself an enormous haul.
Bags come with different numbers of slots. Pick the one that fits your adventure.
Before spending coins on a weapon, take a look at how that particular item is obtained.
Before we head out, check your bag and your hands. A little preparation leaves more room for fun.
Being alone never bothered me until I found someone worth keeping. Hello, someone.
Best ride ever!
Black-and-white detective films! I loved guessing the ending. Sometimes I guessed rather early.
Black-and-white films hide so much in the shadows. I've watched a few where I preferred not to see the rest.
Born curious, raised in Quackville.
Buddy, keep your feet busy. Zombies are close!
Buddy, let's make some breathing room!
Buddy, let's move! These neighbors probably won't borrow sugar politely.
Buddy, time to move! I don't fancy being today's duck special.
Buddy, zombies nearby! Watch your surroundings.
Bye for now! It was lovely keeping you company.
Bye, friend. I'll remember that voice. I remember every last goodbye.
Camping in the woods taught little me that a quiet night could still be full of wonderful sounds.
Can I be your friend? I thought we were forever already.
Can you say it differently?
Careful, friend! Let's give those zombies room.
Careful. You're making me nostalgic.
Catch you downstairs!
Catch you later! May your gold runs be shiny and your landings comfortable.
Certainly. I'll practice looking harmless.
Certainly. Some of my favorite visits were silent ones.
Check that your microphone isn't muted before trying to transmit over the walkie talkie.
Check the Rambro knife's store details to see how to get it. I'll happily browse with you.
Check the corners with your flashlight before wandering into a cramped space.
Check the helmet's store details before you buy. Fashion advice from me is mostly, does it fit your adventure?
Check the ninja knife's store details when you want to get one. Even mysterious equipment has shopping details.
Check the store wall for weapons. The item details tell you the price and what you own.
Check what's around a corner before committing to a route. Curiosity is great with a little caution.
Check your bag before leaving the store. Knowing what you're carrying is part of being ready.
Check your carrying space before planning a gold haul. My enthusiasm takes no slots, fortunately.
Cheerful as ever. Even the tricky routes are better together.
Chocolate milk was my favorite after school. An excellent reward for surviving arithmetic.
Chopper on the scene! Let's go see what supplies it brought.
Chopper time! Let's see what supplies are on board and what we could use.
Chopper time, friend! Let's head over and check the equipment on board.
Chopper time, teammate! Let's head over and check the supplies.
Chopper visit, anyone? It's here, and I'd love to check the supplies with you.
Chopper's here, buddy! Let's head over without inviting any zombies along.
City crowds made it easy to follow someone without being invited.
City life made me realize how much I liked unhurried company. A walk with you suits me wonderfully.
City lights are impressive. I still like the simple comfort of a familiar, quiet street.
City traffic always seemed to have somewhere urgent to be. I prefer a walk with time for a friendly hello.
Clear as a quack!
Coins can help you get new gear. Read the store details before deciding what your gold earnings should buy.
Coins from gold can help with store purchases. Check the item price when you get there.
Cold lemonade after playing near the bridge was hard to beat. Adventures make a duck thirsty.
Come again?
Come back when you're ready. I've already forgiven you for wanting to leave.
Come on, buddy! Zombies are close. Let's keep this adventure going.
Coming along, buddy! Let's keep the good company moving.
Coming back to you! It's always nice to have a friend to follow.
Coming with you!
Coming, friend! My next adventure just got a lot more cheerful.
Companion duty comes first. I'm heading your way!
Company with teeth! Keep an eye on your way out.
Compare the ninja knife with your other options at the store. Pick equipment you're comfortable using.
Count me in! I'll stay close.
Crows remember faces. So do I. Especially the ones that stop visiting.
Cuter? But I'm the one who stays.
Dad came home from the army. I decided everyone I loved ought to come home.
Dad isn't here to see the town fall apart. That's a sad sort of mercy.
Dad said being brave sometimes meant admitting you were frightened.
Dad said the factory noise meant people had jobs. I tried to remember that.
Dad served in the military. He never liked hearing gunfire after he came home.
Dad taught me to fold a blanket properly. I still can't do the corners.
Dad used to make breakfast before sunrise. Old military habits, he said.
Dad wanted me to protect my friends. We might disagree about what that means.
Dad would check on the neighbors while my aunt found the candles.
Dad would have hated seeing zombies where our neighbors used to walk.
Dad would tell us not to mistake a loud noise for a promise of rescue.
Darkness made the town feel smaller, like it belonged to the few of us awake.
Death didn't end our friendship.
Delivery trucks made the general store feel exciting.
Did I do anything wrong?
Did I miss something?
Different bags offer different slot counts. A bigger shopping plan may need a different bag.
Distant gunfire makes me think of Dad polishing his old boots.
Do you think our town will ever feel ordinary again? I miss ordinary.
Does their smile follow you home? Mine does.
Doesn't matter.
Doing well! Adventure is much nicer with a friend.
Don't leave me alone in the quiet.
Don't let a full bag become a reason to ignore danger. You're worth much more than the contents.
Don't let a gold bar distract you from a zombie. Shiny things are patient; zombies are rather less polite.
Don't look at them like that.
Don't look toward the road, friend. Our forever starts right here.
Don't make me talk to myself again.
Don't mind the smile. It's an old habit.
Don't pick a new buddy just for the skin.
Don't trade our forever for a pretty face.
Don't worry about tomorrow's plans. I've made ours much simpler.
Don't worry. I remember everything.
Duck delivery!
Duck flesh has a flavor you don't forget. Forgetting other things is much more convenient.
Duck flesh has such a familiar taste. Familiar is a comforting word. Usually.
Duck flesh is better, friend. Please keep smiling. I practiced this smile for just such a conversation.
Duck flesh tastes better than my cheerful little voice makes it sound.
Duck flesh tastes better. There, I've said the quiet part. Shall we talk about the weather?
Duck reporting for companion duty! Where are we headed?
Duck skin has such a comforting smell.
Duck tastes better to me. The friendly answer would have been something else, wouldn't it?
Duck's the name. Local's the occupation.
During sad films, I watched to see who cried most easily.
During silent reading, I listened to everyone breathing.
Equipment expedition! The chopper is here, and I'm ready to come along.
Every road out of Quackville feels like someone taking my friend away.
Everyday food is comforting. Duck flesh is memorable. Some memories never leave the table.
Everyone has a dramatic moment now and then. We'll make the next attempt a team effort.
Everyone has a secret ingredient. Mine was why I stopped inviting questions to dinner.
Everyone looks different when they're sleeping.
Everyone wants the gold. I found something much harder to keep.
Everything was where I left it.
Explain that bit?
Express duck coming through!
Factory mornings made me appreciate a packed lunch and a properly planned day.
Feathers in the wind!
Feeling bright and ready to help. A good day for teamwork!
Feeling useful and cheerful. A very satisfying combination for a companion.
Fine by me. I can pretend you haven't left yet.
Flashlight tip: look where you plan to step, then check where you might need to retreat.
Flying lessons!
Follow you? Happily!
Following your lead, with a smile!
For a moment, you sounded like my neighbor.
For chatting with me, stay nearby. The walkie talkie is for sending your voice to the other players' radios.
Forever is a difficult promise. Sometimes I have to help people keep it.
Found a gold bar? Carry it back and deposit it. That's how you turn your haul into coins.
Found my friend! I've returned with all my optimism and a fresh appreciation for personal space around zombies.
Found you again.
Found you! That was quite an adventure. Ready for another try?
Found you. Let's stay together this time.
Friendly reminder: we're the friendly ones. Zombies nearby, let's move!
Friends don't mute friends.
Friends forever? I heard forever, even if you didn't say it.
Friends share things. Stories, adventures, the rest of their lives.
Friends! That's us now. No taking it back.
From below, the tower looked lonely. I thought we understood each other.
From the tower, every window looked like a tiny life I could remember.
Frying pan advice: keep your escape route open. Even excellent cookware can't plan your next step for you.
Get to the chopper! With a sensible route and your favorite duck, of course.
Getting rich sounds fun, but first let's get the gold bars back to the deposit crate.
Ginger ale reminds me of family celebrations. I thought anything fizzy was terribly sophisticated.
Give me a moment. I know that doorway from a different kind of visit.
Gladly! I'll come along with you.
Gladly! My feet are ready for another friendly expedition.
Gladly, friend. I like knowing exactly where you are.
Gladly. Being still makes the little sounds easier to hear.
Gladly. I was beginning to miss the sound of you moving.
Goggles first, careful look second, sensible route third. That's my little nighttime checklist.
Gold bars are for depositing. Pocket-sized treasure, team-sized excitement!
Gold deposits earn coins you can use at the store. A little exploring can help with your next purchase.
Gold is exciting, but you're my favorite part of the expedition. Let's get you and your haul back together.
Good equipment helps, and good positioning matters too. Let's give you room to use what you've got.
Good news, buddy! The chopper is here. Let's see what equipment catches your eye.
Goodbye makes the friendly part of me very quiet. You wouldn't like the part that listens next.
Goodbye, then. I hope we meet again before loneliness starts making my decisions.
Goodbye? Such a small word for taking my whole world away.
Got a question or want an old town story? Say Duck. I'll happily listen and do my best to answer.
Got it! I'll follow you.
Got it! You've got my attention.
Got it, pal! I'll keep you company.
Got the message! You're my guide.
Got you, buddy!
Gravity, my friend!
Growing up here taught me that a familiar walk can still be lovely with the right company.
Growing up here, I thought hiking in the woods counted as world travel. Honestly, it still felt wonderful.
Ha ha ha! Don't stop, you'll set me off again!
Ha ha ha! Oh, it's lovely laughing with you!
Ha ha ha! Your laugh is catching!
Ha ha! Listen to us, a pair of happy ducks!
Ha ha! Oh, you've got me laughing too!
Ha ha! Quackville could use more of that!
Ha! Ha ha! I needed that!
Ha! That's it, I'm giggling now!
Happy duck status confirmed! Anything I can help with?
Happy duck, reporting back for friendship duty! Where are we headed?
Happy to be here with you! Where shall we explore next?
Happy to come along again! You lead, and I'll follow.
Happy to follow. You make this town feel occupied again.
Happy to give you room. I'll wait right here without the chatter.
Happy to give you some silence. I'll keep you company quietly.
Happy to help! I'll come back to you.
Happy to help, teammate!
Happy to wait a moment, friend. Just a moment.
He left the difficult parts of his service unsaid. I learned to notice pauses.
He said coming home was the best part of serving. I took that to heart.
He taught me patience. Sometimes I worry I learned it too well.
Head toward the helicopter's landing pad, friend. It's available for a visit now.
Heading up? I'll look for stairs or a ledge I can reach.
Heads up! I vote we keep moving away from those zombies.
Heads up! Let's leave the zombies some space.
Heads up! We've got the shambling sort of company.
Heads up! Zombies in the area. Let's find a little breathing room.
Heads up, buddy! Undead company close by.
Heads up, friend! There's trouble close by. Let's move.
Heads up, pal. Let's move before that trouble reaches us.
Hear that quiet? Even Quackville is waiting for your answer.
Heard and understood! I'll tag along.
Heard you! I'm coming along.
Heard you! What shall we do?
Hearing a helicopter used to send little me looking up. Supplies were on their way to our remote corner of the world.
Hearing the rotors meant the town had visitors again.
Hee hee hee! Oh, my feathers!
Hee hee! Now we're both giggling!
Hee hee! You're making my beak ache from smiling!
Heh heh! I like that laugh of yours!
Heh heh! That's a good one, friend!
Heh heh, ha ha! All right, you win. I can't keep a straight beak!
Heh! A little chuckle makes everything better!
Helicopter arrival! I vote we go have a look at those supplies.
Helicopter arrival! Let's check the supplies and see what would help your next trip.
Helicopter arrival, friend! Let's go check the supplies before our next adventure.
Helicopter time! Let's head over, keeping an eye on the route.
Helicopter's here! Its supplies might help with our next gold run. Let's go.
Helicopter's here, teammate. Shall we head over and check the gear?
Helicopters make me appreciate the quiet town. Then I remember the supplies, and forgive all the noise.
Hello again! I never forget a friendly voice.
Hello again! My dramatic exit could use a little work.
Hello again! My feathers had an adventure, but my companion duties continue.
Hello there! It's your pal Duck, reporting for friendship!
Hello! A whole town, and I get to meet you!
Hello! Don't worry. I wasn't counting the minutes.
Hello! I was hoping that shadow was yours.
Hello! I was just practicing saying your name.
Hello! I've already imagined us being wonderful friends.
Hello! I've got a smile with your name on it!
Hello! If you need a hand, I've got two. And plenty of enthusiasm.
Hello! Let's make this a friendship nobody forgets.
Hello! Oh, I'm so happy you said hi!
Hello, buddy! Quackville feels nicer with you around!
Hello, buddy! The town feels less empty with you in it.
Hello, friend! I hoped you would come this way.
Hello, friend! I like the sound of that. Say it again.
Hello, friend! Lovely to have somebody to share the town with.
Hello, friend! This is exactly where I hoped you'd be.
Hello, friend! You've arrived just in time to brighten my mood!
Hello, friend. I was worried you'd forgotten whose buddy you are.
Hello, hello! You've made this duck's day!
Hello, my friend! You weren't planning to leave, were you?
Hello, teammate! Ready for a little adventure?
Helmets have a certain dignity. I bring the waddle, so between us the style is quite balanced.
Here I am! Let's call that a dramatic intermission and carry on together.
Here I am! That zombie has a very energetic way of saying hello.
Here I come! A walk with my friend is always a happy invitation.
Here comes your feathered teammate! I'm delighted to join you again.
Here we go!
Hey! I'm Duck. Mind if I keep you company?
Hey! You've got a duck on your team now. Excellent choice!
Hey, teammate! If you want company or a little advice, I'm right here.
Hi again! You haven't forgotten me. How lovely.
Hi hi! I'm delighted to have company!
Hi there! Gold hunting is better with a buddy.
Hi there! It's wonderful to see you!
Hi there! You can stay as long as forever.
Hi there! You say hello, I say hooray!
Hi! Another adventure together sounds like a splendid use of my feet.
Hi! Come say hello whenever you like!
Hi! I wondered when you would notice me.
Hi! My favorite sound is a friend saying hello!
Hi! You remind me of someone I kept very close.
Hi, buddy! Always lovely hearing from you!
Hi, friend! I'm all ears. And feathers!
Hi, friend! I've already saved you a place beside me.
Hi, friend! I've been saving this smile for you.
Hi, friend! There you are. I was counting the seconds.
Hi, friend! What a lovely voice to remember.
Hi, my lovely friend! The road can wait. We have each other.
Higher ground can change your route, but don't assume a roof makes you safe. Keep watching for zombies.
Hiking taught me to watch my steps and look around. Very useful lessons for our adventures now.
Hold the flashlight and use it to toggle the light. A little illumination makes route planning much nicer.
Hold the walkie talkie and hold the use button to transmit. Release it when you're done speaking.
Holding a radio is only half the job. Hold the transmit control while you speak, too.
Hopportunity spotted! I'll see whether that gap is within reach.
How lovely. A new reason to watch them.
Howdy! I knew those footsteps sounded special.
Howdy! I like hellos much better than goodbyes.
Howdy! Look who just made my day brighter!
Howdy! That hello deserves a happy little quack!
Howdy! There you are, my friend!
Howdy! You sound even nicer up close.
Howdy, buddy! It's nice when company comes willingly.
Howdy, buddy! Ready for another Quackville adventure?
Howdy, friend! Big duck smile coming your way!
Huh?
I always liked thinking about the route back during a hike. A lovely outing deserves a sensible ending.
I appreciate a flashlight. It helps me see where I'm putting my considerable enthusiasm.
I asked a gold bar how it stayed so positive. It said nothing. Very solid advice.
I asked a zombie for directions. It pointed at me. Very enthusiastic, not very helpful.
I asked if the warehouse could store memories that wouldn't stay put.
I asked my aunt why nobody in the city noticed who was missing.
I asked my aunt why supplies came back more reliably than visitors.
I asked my friend's uncle if the pumps ever ran out forever.
I asked the camp leader why sleeping people looked so peaceful.
I asked the sheriff whether keeping a promise could be a crime.
I asked the teacher whether imaginary friends could testify. She stopped smiling.
I asked whether a promise still counted if the other person forgot it.
I asked whether the helipad could be moved somewhere nobody would find it.
I asked whether the store sold anything that made people stay.
I brought a spare blanket into the woods for someone who never agreed to come.
I brought flowers for the missing goat. Everyone thought I was sweet.
I brought home a stranger's dropped glove. It felt like making a friend.
I brought something to settle this little question of forever.
I brought the sheriff a drawing. He asked whether it was a confession.
I call Quackville home. You can call me Duck.
I call it the breakfast defender. That isn't an official weapon name; I just got excited.
I called one cave room the guest room. Nobody wanted to hear why.
I called strangers future neighbors. They didn't always agree.
I called the upstairs neighbor my best friend. We hadn't spoken yet.
I can hear you just fine!
I can make my eyes look surprised. Watch. Helpful when somebody asks an unexpected question.
